To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cilia of the embryonic node drive left-right asymmetry by propelling fluid around the node.
the cilia that propel the node are monocilia and that they are required for left-right axis formation.

ciliary dynein and kinesin are required to drive leftward flow in the node, that the leftward flow is required to establish left-right asymmetry in the mouse embryo, and that the left-right asymmetry of cilia is required for the establishment of left-right asymmetries in the rest of the mouse embryo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which cilia generate the fluid flow that establishes left-right asymmetry, and with the role of monocilia in the development of the mammalian embryo.
understanding how ciliary function is coordinated to generate a left-right asymmetry.
the molecular basis of left-right asymmetries in mammals, and how they are established in the embryo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cilia are required to establish left-right asymmetry in the embryo.
the cilia that propel the node are not the same cilia that propel sperm, and the cilia that drive the left-right asymmetry are not the same as those that drive the flow of cerebrospinal fluid.
the left-right axis is formed by a cilia-driven flow of extracellular fluid in a leftward direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cilia are required for left-right determination, and that the monocilia on the node are responsible for initiating left-right asymmetry.
cilia are required for normal left-right asymmetry, and that the monocilia of the node are required for the establishment of left-right asymmetries.
ciliary motility is required for the generation of left-right asymmetries in the mouse embryo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cilia that propel embryonic development are not conventional ciliated cells, but monocilia, and that the cilia on the mouse node drive net leftward fluid flow and thereby initiate left-right asymmetries in the mouse embryo.
the molecular motors dynein and kinesin are essential for the generation of the left-right asymmetry that is a fundamental feature of the vertebrate body plan.
the molecular motors that drive cilia are essential for left-right patterning.
